la:verb:obicio.html:
ōbĭcĭo and objĭcĭo, jēci, jectum, 3 (cf. abicio, etc.;
perf. subj. objexim, : objexis,), v. a.
ob-jacio
, to throw or put before or towards, to throw to, to hold before or out, to offer, present, expose; constr. usu. aliquid (aliquem) alicui, or simply aliquid; but sometimes also, instead of the dat., with pro aliquā re, contra, ad, in aliquid;v.the foll. passages; also with adversus; v. Drak. (syn. oppono).
Lit.: ei nos Glaucomam ob oculos obiciemus,: si alia quae obiciant non habuerint,: cibum canibus,: parricidae corpus feris,: offam (Cerbero),: pisces diripiunt carnes objectas, (Jan, abiectas): argentum, to throw to one, .—Esp., to throw to the wild beasts in the circus: aliquem feris,; ; ; et saep.: vivos homines laniandos obicere,: florem veteris vini naribus,to hold before, present to,; ; : si tale visum objectum est a deo dormienti,brought before, presented to,; cf. ; : huic (sicae) ego vos obici pro me non sum passus,to be exposed,: exercitum tantae magnitudinis flumini,: ne objexis manum,don't raise your hand,. —
In partic., to throw or place before by way of defence or hinderance; to cast in the way, set against, oppose: Alpium vallum contra ascensum transgressionemque Gallorum ... obicio et oppono,: carros pro vallo,: ericium portis,: faucibus portūs navem submersam,; 3, 66: se hostium telis,: se ei objecit,: maximo aggere objecto,.—Esp. of arms: objecta tela perfregit,: scutum,: hastas,: clipeosque ad tela sinistris Protecti obiciunt,oppose,: objecit sese ad currum,threw himself before the chariot,.—
Trop.
In gen., to throw before or over, to put or bring before, to present; to give up, expose to any thing; and, in gen., to bring upon one, to impart, superinduce, cause, occasion, etc.: noctem peccatis et fraudibus obice nubem,: nubem oculis,: plerique victi et debilitati objectā specie voluptatis,: consulem morti,to deliver up, abandon,: obicitur (consulatus) contionibus seditiosorum ... ad omne denique periculum,.—With ad, . —With in: numquam me pro salute vestrā in tot ac tantas dimicationes ... objecissem,: obicere se in impetus profligatorum hominum,. —With adversus: se unico consule objecto adversus tribuniciam potestatem perlatam legem esse,: qui multa Thebano populo acerba objecit funera, hasbrought on, i. e. caused, , moram alicui, ; : ut hanc laetitiam nec opinanti primus obicerem, that I might have set before him, i. e. prepared for him, : alicui eam mentem, ut patriam prodat,to suggest,: alicui lucrum,to procure,: sollicitudinem,to cause,: terrorem hosti,: spem,: furorem alicui objecit,: rabiem canibus,.—Pass., to be occasioned, to befall, happen, occur to one: mihi mala res obicitur aliqua,: malum mihi obicitur,; cf. : obicitur animo metus,.—
To put in the way, interpose: omnis exceptio interponitur a reo,: cui dilatoria obicitur exceptio,.—
In partic., to throw out against one, to taunt, reproach, or upbraid with any thing, as a crime (cf.: criminor, exprobro): facinora,: alicui multa probra,: ignobilitatem alicui,: obicit mihi, me ad Baias fuisse,: parcius ista viris obicienda memento,.—With quod: Cato objecit ut probrum M. Nobiliori, quod is in provinciam poëtas duxisset,; : furta, Auct. Dom. 35, 93: eloquentiam ut vitium, Cic. ap. : crimen,.—With de, to reproach one respecting, on account of any thing: de Cispio mihi igitur obicies? etc.,; Brut. et Cass. ap. . —In pass.: nam quod objectum est de pudicitiā, etc.,.—Hence, objec-tus, a, um, P. a.
Lying before or opposite: insula objecta Alexandriae,: silva pro nativo muro,: flumina,: Cyprus Syriae objecta,.—
Exposed; constr. with dat. or ad: objectus fortunae,: invidiae,: ad omnes casus,.—
Subst.: objecta, ōrum, n., charges, accusations: de objectis non confiteri,: objecta vel negare vel defendere vel minuere,: objecta diluere,; ; cf. .

la:adv:obiter.html:
ŏb-ĭter,
adv., on the way, in going or passing along (except in Laber., not anteAug.; cf. P. Augustus found fault with Tiberius for using per viam instead of obiter, Charis. l. l.).
Lit.: obiter leget aut scribet,on the way,: rotae, quas aqua verset obiter et molat,as it flows along,; cf. ; ; .—
Transf.
By the way, in passing, incidentally: interrogo ego: Quot estis? obiterque per rimam speculari coepit,: faciem linit,: ne in hoc quidem tam molesto tacebant officio, sed obiter cantabant,: saevire,: licet obiter vanitatem magicam hic quoque coarguere,: dictum sit,; ; —
Forthwith, straightway, immediately (very rare): ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ inibi, obiter, Gloss. Philox.: reducant,: ut obiter revertantur, Auct.
